title: Welcome to my blog
text: Welcome to my blog! I’ve decided to start writing occasionally about my work and interests in infectious disease modelling.

title: Welcome to my blog
text:
What to expect
I plan to write about:

Research updates: Sharing thoughts on ongoing projects and new publications
Methods and tutorials: Occasional posts about modelling approaches and tools
Reflections: Thoughts on academia, collaboration, and the research process
Community: Updates from INDEMIC and other collaborative efforts

title: Welcome to my blog
text:
Why start a blog?
As researchers, we often focus on formal publications, but I think there’s value in sharing more informal thoughts and updates. It’s also a way to document my journey and connect with others interested in similar topics.
Feel free to reach out if you’d like to discuss any of the topics I write about!

Hello! I am an infectious disease epidemiologist and modeller. My research focuses on developing and applying statistical and mathematical models to understand infectious disease dynamics and inform public health policy. I have worked on malaria, dengue, COVID-19, and diphtheria.
I am currently a Research Fellow at Saw Swee Hock School of Public Health, National University of Singapore, MLGH-SG group.

title: News & Updates
text:
June 2026: Our new paper on the usability of epidemic forecasts for policymakers is out, led by Paula Christen and OJ Watson
May 2026: Attended PREPARE - TF READI: Policy-driven Infectious Diseases Modelling Workshop. What a great meeting! A lot was discussed on how to use modelling for policy and how policymakers and modellers should work together. I had the opportunity to talk about my experience working with policymakers in Indonesia and moderating a fireside chat with Azra Ghani!
May 2026: Went to Krabi, Thailand to attend MIDSEA Fiesta where we discussed the future of our beloved modeling community!
March 2026: Our paper on dengue transmission heterogenenity across in Indonesia is out
January 2026: Happy new year! (Finally) Updated this personal website

title: News & Updates
text:
2025

November 2025: Teaching assistant for Modelling and Analysis of Serological Data: An Introductory Short Course (Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
October 2025: Second Modra Workshop (Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam)
September 2025: First MODRA workshop (Bangkok, Thailand)
July 2025: Got accepted for MORU-OUCRU Discovery Research Academy program (MODRA) cohort 2!
June 2025: MIDSEA Summer School 2025 in Indonesia! I taught inference track and assisted our brilliant local organiser from Dept. of Mathematics, UGM to ensure things were run smoothly (Yogyakarta, Indonesia)
April 2025: Participated in dengue multisource suveillance workshop which is the follow up from the 2024 one (Semarang, Indonesia)
February 2025: Gave a half-day online workshop on ‘Modeling Infectious Disease Transmission to Mitigate Potential Outbreak Threats’, which is part of GAMA-ICTM 2025 conference (Yogyakarta, Indonesia)

title: News & Updates
text:
2024

November 2024: Participated in Collaboratory Workshop: Dengue Analytics Workshop (Berlin, Germany)
November 2024: Participated in the Infectious Disease Modelling Conference 2024 in Bangkok as part of the early career researcher (ECR) committee (Bangkok, Thailand)
August 2024: Participated and presented in Isaac Newton Institute’s Modelling and inference for pandemic preparedness (Cambridge, the UK)
July 2024: Participated in dengue multisource suveillance workshop (Semarang, Indonesia)
June 2024: Participated in MIDSEA Summer School 2024 (Quy Nhon, Vietnam). I taught the inference track for one day and then took the geospatial modelling track
April 2024: Joined Saw Swee Hock School of Public Health, National University of Singapore as Research Fellow
February 2024: Left Imperial College London (and London) after 5.5 years

title: Resources
text:
I made these resources mainly in Indonesian to increase accessibility for Indonesians wanting to learn about infectious disease modelling. I tried my best to attribute sources within each material.
